summary: ```markdown # CLO Skills Mini Class - Adjusting the Strap through the Eyelet Buckle ## Introduction Hi, everyone. This is Tips and Tricks. Today, I will show you how to make a pocket pocket strap. Like the pocket pocket, we also use the pocket pocket to make a pocket pocket strap. ## Understanding the Pocket Pocket Strap We can see the effect of the pocket pocket strap on the pocket pocket strap. Here is a real hole-in-the-box effect made by using duplicate simulation. In the case of duplicate simulation, there is a mutual effect between the board and the duplicate. Currently, duplicate simulation can only be used in CPU simulation. Therefore, if you need to use duplicate simulation, it is recommended to switch to CPU simulation. ## Setting Up the Simulation We can see the hole-in-the-box effect on the left side. It involves passing a complete rope through this duplicate. Next, we need to pass this rope on the right side through a wooden buckle. To make it easier to operate, it is recommended that you first divide this rope into three parts. ### Dividing the Rope You can use the hook and loop tool to divide the board. Divide it into three parts to make it easier to pass through the board. Then, add a fixed pin on the divided board and turn on the simulation. Adding a fixed pin here will help to adjust the shape of the board and the position of the moving board. ## Adding Components Next, add a wooden buckle. If you already have a corresponding duplicate solution, you can add it. You can also find a similar component in the CLOAD library or CONNECT. Add it to the 3D window and use it. Here, we can copy the wooden buckle that we already have in the object window and drag it into the 3D window to add it. ### Positioning the Wooden Buckle We can use the positioning ball directly to adjust the position of the wooden buckle, making the top board pass through the ring in the wooden buckle. You can see that this board has actually passed through the wooden buckle. At this point, you can turn on the simulation to observe its buckle effect. ## Managing Duplication Conflicts You can see that the board and the duplicate are mutually effective at this time. The board will hang the duplicate, similar to the real buckle effect. We need to pay attention to duplicate simulation, as there is a conflict between the board and the duplicate. Therefore, in the process of making, if the board and the duplicate pass through, you can use the selection tool to adjust the board's position. ### Adjusting the Board Position If you see the area where there is a pass-through, you can use the selection tool to select it. Then, use the positioning ball to adjust its position. So, the upper part of the wooden buckle is done. Next, you can adjust the remaining two parts of this strap, as we have increased the thickness of the board to make it easier to visualize the looping effect of the wooden buckle. ## Final Adjustments You can switch to the clothing suspension type and switch to the texture surface. Here, we can see the pass-through effect of the thickness of the suspension. Let me remind you that if there is any deformation during the simulation process, it can also be adjusted in the right-hand attribute editor by modifying its rigidity. The larger the rigidity, the more difficult it is to deform the duplicate. You can also adjust the thickness of the conflict and the size of the gap between the duplicate and the board. ### Arranging the Strap To create the looping effect of the strap, arrange a small board in the position of the looping on the wooden buckle and adjust its position through the positioning ball to pass through the wooden buckle on one side. You can also switch to a different angle to check the effect of the board. ### Adding Inner Lines Here we have arranged the position on one side. We can add an inner line to it by clicking on the 3D window. Then, use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw an inner line. After that, select the folding arrangement tool in the 3D window and choose the inner line to fold. At the bottom, you can add a new inner line and fold it, checking for surface area and adjusting the folding angle as needed. ## Completing the Strap At this point, the effect of the front buckle is also done. We can now place the other two side boards in the state of opening the simulation. Use the fixed needle to move the board position to the part that needs to be connected together. ### Finalizing the Design Once done, remove all the pins on the board. Now, tumbling the board together prepares it for the title. Open the simulation, check the cross-section of the board and the component, and adjust the cross-section area between them by selecting the grid tool. You can also select the cross-section area in the 2D window frame and adjust its location using the positioning ball. ## Merging the Boards Since the rope belt is a complete board, we need to merge these three boards together to form a complete belt. Here, you can change the angle of these two cross-section lines to 180 degrees or delete these two internal lines. ### Rendering the Final Product Finally, render the clothing type and change it to the surface of the dense pattern. This way, the thickness of the rope belt can also be displayed. Let's start the simulation again. This completes the adjustment of the strap and demonstrates the real effect of the cross-section. ```
